html:
A battle on 9 August 378 near Adrianople, today's Edirne in European Turkey, in which Gothic rebels destroyed an eastern Roman army and killed the emperor Valens.

The Goths had been let into the empire two years before and then rose against harsh treatment. Valens did not wait for help from his nephew Gratian, who was coming from the west. He attacked the Gothic wagon camp led by Fritigern on a hot day after a long march. Gothic horsemen returning from foraging struck the Roman flank, and the army was surrounded. About two thirds of it died. The officer Ammianus Marcellinus wrote the main account.

The defeat was a turning point. Theodosius I could not drive the Goths out, and in 382 settled them inside the empire as allies under their own leaders. Many historians date the start of the fall of the western empire from this day.
sum: A battle on 9 August 378 near Adrianople, today's Edirne in European Turkey, in which Gothic rebels destroyed an eastern Roman army and killed the emperor Valens.
